title: Now Satan Comes with Dreadful Roar
description: Now Satan Comes with Dreadful Roar in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 157, headed “The same”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now Sa-tan comes with dread-ful roar, And threat-ens to de-stroy; He wor-ries whom he can't de-vour With a ma-li-cious joy.

lines: Now Satan comes with dreadful roar,
He worries whom he can't devour
Ye sons of God, oppose his rage,
Thus did our dearest Lord engage
But the old serpent lurks within
Fly from the false deceiver's tongue,
Our parents found the snare too strong,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
